findings.location: Increment C — Affected areas and Steps 1–3 (lines 132–140); Increment B Step 1 (lines 117–121)
findings.problem: The plan removes `init` but does not explicitly update the recall-memory skill or its guidance test. B explicitly preserves the skill text that says “Never run `init` or `mine`”, while the current guidance test pins that wording. This conflicts with completion criterion 4’s requirement that no test, spec, or doc offer `init`.
findings.suggestion: Add the skill and `test_mempalace_guidance.py` to C, and specify replacement wording that prohibits the remaining owner-run commands (`mine` and `sync`) without naming removed `init`; update B so its preservation requirement applies only until C.

findings.location: Increment D — “The lock” and D Step 1 (lines 163–177)
findings.problem: Every mine/sync run is specified to lock `.workbench/local/mempalace.lock`, but the plan does not define or test safe creation of the untracked `local` directory when it is absent. A fresh clone normally has no untracked `local` directory, and criterion 1 expressly treats that absence as valid. As written, terminal owner runs can fail before starting the program, undermining the per-clone/no-setup goal.
findings.suggestion: Specify a no-follow, descriptor-relative creation path for a missing `local` directory (with its required mode and refusal cases), or narrowly state and implement an alternative safe lock location. Add tests for terminal and ask-level runs from a clone with no `local` directory, plus link/non-directory contention cases.

summary: Two implementation gaps remain: the init-removal guidance contradicts its completion criterion, and the lock design does not handle a fresh clone without `.workbench/local`.
